task_summary: Read an Excel data file and a PDF background file, then compute (Player 1 wins) minus (Player 2 wins) from paired odd/even game rows, and write the numeric answer to a file.
decomposition_rationale: This task involves three distinct concerns: (1) reading the PDF to understand the data context/column meanings, (2) loading and analyzing the Excel data with correct index-parity logic for paired game comparisons, and (3) writing the result. Since the PDF reading is a simple prerequisite and the core logic is a single analytical pipeline, two skills suffice: one for PDF context extraction and one for the Excel-based match analysis and output.

skills.name: evo-pdf-context-extractor
skills.description: Extracts text content from a PDF file using pypdf 5.x to understand the background context, column definitions, and scoring rules for the data analysis task.
skills.responsibility: Read and parse PDF files, returning extracted text for interpretation of data semantics and question context.
dr_sections: 3. Extracting Unstructured Data: PDF Parsing with `pypdf` (5.1.0)
3.1 Migration from PyPDF2 and Import Semantics

skills.name: evo-excel-match-analyzer
skills.description: Loads an Excel file, splits rows by parity into Player 1 (odd-numbered games) and Player 2 (even-numbered games), pairs them for head-to-head comparison, computes win counts, and writes the final numeric result to a text file.
skills.responsibility: Excel data ingestion, index-parity slicing with correct 0-indexed vs 1-indexed mapping, reset_index alignment for vectorized comparison, win/loss tallying, and strict output formatting.
dr_sections: 2. Advanced Ingestion of Large Excel Files
4. Game/Match Comparison: Analytical Patterns and Index Parity
5. Determining Match Winners and Edge Case Handling
5.2 Pitfalls in Row Filtering and Comparisons
7. Synthesis: A Comprehensive Reusable Utility Class
